title: What Does Retrieved Memory Buy? Accuracy, Evidence and Write Cost
research_question: How do file-based project memory and hybrid retrieval compare in answer accuracy and total model cost under equal context-character budgets?

subsections.title: File-Based Project Memory
subsections.goal: The baseline is the actual ProjectMemoryRail. Facts are written to an isolated JIUWENSWARM.md file. Its prompt includes file metadata and is truncated to the full-section character budget. Both arms receive the same facts, questions, model, system prompt and no tools. This is not a retrieval-augmented embedding baseline.

subsections.title: Hybrid Selection from Working Memory
subsections.goal: EnhancedMemoryRail writes completed user-assistant exchanges to process-local L1 memory. The experiment uses lexical Jaccard similarity combined with temporal decay, access frequency and importance, rather than learned embeddings. Selected memories are assembled under the same full-section character budget. The architecture has L2/L3 classes, but this Rail does not route writes there, persist them across process restarts or synchronize a team. MemGPT is conceptual context, not an implemented or tested baseline.

subsections.title: Isolation and Cost Accounting
subsections.goal: Each public-data question has its own fact episode and fresh agents. Baseline writes facts to disk; enhanced performs model-backed memory-writing conversations. The formal question uses a new conversation ID. The runner verifies isolated query history and actual memory injection, alternates arm order across questions, and records both query usage and memory-write usage. Latency including writes is amortized over paired observations. Correctness is accepted-answer string matching; evidence recall requires the complete target fact to survive prompt truncation.
